citation.title: Main ion and impurity edge profile evolution across the L- to H-mode transition on DIII-D
citation.authors: S. R. Haskey, B. A. Grierson, C. Chrystal, A. Ashourvan, K. H. Burrell, R. J. Groebner, E. A. Belli, L. Stagner, D. Battaglia, T. Stoltzfus-Dueck, A. Bortolon
citation.doi_or_arxiv: unknown; DOIs in the reference list belong to cited works

scope_read.limitations: Preprint layout without journal metadata. Figure values were read from plots. DIII-D only, with two shots (164436 and 164988).

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The D+ versus C6+ temperature difference is largest at the separatrix.
claim_checks.source_finding: In the ITER-baseline H-mode, the D+ temperature falls below half the C6+ temperature near the separatrix. In the low-power L-mode, the two temperatures agree within error bars except near the separatrix, where the gap grows slightly.
claim_checks.locator: p1 Abstract; p4 Sec II.B, Fig.4(c), Fig.5(b); p7 Sec III
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Direct main-ion spectroscopy on DIII-D found edge deuterium temperatures below the carbon CER values, with the gap reaching more than a factor of two near the separatrix in a high-power H-mode.
claim_checks.qualification: Shows a measured gap, not a general factor. The authors call atomic-physics cooling the likely cause. They also list in-out asymmetry, orbit-tail and Zeeman effects as candidates; no mechanism was isolated.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: A difference is also reported at the pedestal top.
claim_checks.source_finding: In the low-power H-mode, the D+ temperature is about 70 eV lower, roughly halfway between the C6+ and electron temperatures. The ITER case shows a similar difference inside the pedestal top. Unapplied Zeeman estimates could reduce the impurity-ion gap by about 30 eV. After the L-H transition the gap widens within the 5 ms integration time.
claim_checks.locator: p4 Sec II.B, Fig.4(d), Fig.5(b); p5 Sec II.B, Fig.3(e-f)
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Smaller but resolvable differences of tens of eV were reported inside the pedestal top in H-mode, and part of this may be spectroscopic in origin.
claim_checks.qualification: In L-mode the temperatures were coupled within error bars inside the edge. The magnitude depends on regime and on the Zeeman treatment.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Carbon CES temperature should be treated as a conventional label rather than the bulk-ion temperature.
claim_checks.source_finding: The authors note that ion temperatures are commonly assumed equal and argue that the observed differences make direct main-ion measurement important.
claim_checks.locator: p4 Sec II.B; p7 Sec III
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Because impurity and main-ion temperatures can differ in the edge, we treat reported carbon CES temperature as a diagnostic label rather than as the bulk-ion temperature.
claim_checks.qualification: The main-ion CER values are a modeled measurement, not independent truth. Results are from DIII-D and say nothing about the KSTAR chord.

input_target_timing.inputs: not_applicable (not an estimator paper; CER spectra with 5 ms integration, analysed offline)
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: Compares two spectroscopic measurements; neither is presented as independent physical truth.

validation.unknowns: Uncertainty in the temperature difference is read only from figure error bars.

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: 5 ms CER integration time; the paper states this was too slow to resolve the transition event itself.
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Any real-time use or report latency.
runtime_or_deployment.locator: p2 Sec II; p4 Sec II.A

forbidden_inferences: The KSTAR carbon CES chord shows a similar offset or ratio.
The factor of two applies at the pedestal top.
A cause has been identified (charge-exchange cooling is the authors' suggestion).
The paper concerns estimation or nowcasting.
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. It motivates defining the target as the reported impurity CES value and does not compete with the estimator.
followup_sources_if_material: Ref.14/17 (Haskey et al., MICER edge method)
Ref.39 (Chrystal et al., edge CER upgrade)
